chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Ibn Bukayr said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man divorces his wife and calls two just witnesses to accept her waiting period, he does not have the right to divorce her again until her waiting period expires, unless he revokes the divorce (reconciles with her).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on revoking a divorce after witnesses have been called?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the distinction between the pronouncement of divorce and its finalization, emphasizing that the husband retains the right of revocation (ruju') during the 'iddah period provided two just witnesses attest to the event. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the procedural requirement of witness testimony to validate the commencement of the waiting period, ensuring the woman's rights are protected before the divorce becomes irrevocable. It highlights the dynamic nature of the 'iddah as a window for reconciliation rather than an immediate severance of marital ties.
